doc.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013

title: First gig with Freddie Hubbard, Greensboro, November 1982
summary: Allen recalls his first day with Hubbard, the stylish dress, Hubbard cursing out the band for forgetting tunes, and the east-coast and west-coast bands.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So I’ll never forget, one of the highlights, there was really two highlights in rehearsal. One, to see how he was dressed. He’d come to the rehearsal with jeans on, a short olive green suede jacket with a silk scarf around with beige suede cowboy boots and a hat. And I was like, God, he’s clean. This is just a rehearsal, right? He was clean. He was casual, and real clean. So it was my first day in the band, and the other cats had been in the band for a little while. And so one of the other highlights was getting to see him curse out the rest of the band, because they couldn’t remember some of the tunes. Freddie was like, “This young boy’s first day on the gig drummer, he know all these tunes — how you all not remember these tunes?” I was like, “Yeah, tell ‘em, that’s right.” And what I learned for the next eight years Freddie’s mindset was if he called a tune one time and you played it with him one time, your job was to never, ever forget it. And that was kind of how I was raised musically from playing with Freddie. Now, he might call a tune today and might not call it again for two and a half months. And the problem with that, I guess some of it seems a little unfair. Freddie had a lot of different bands. So he had an east coast band and he had a west coast band. And so after a couple of years I was in both bands. But he would play different tunes with the east coast band and the west coast band. So we’d get on a gig and Freddie’d call, “Skagly.” I said, “Freddie, that’s the west coast.” “Why? They’re supposed to know it.” And these guys are looking at me like — but his mindset was if you play it with me once don’t ever forget it. If you say you want to be in the band, learn the music.
